title: Halobacteriovorax sp. GFR8 Growth and Aquarium Inoculation Protocol
author: Lauren Speare
materials: Day 1: Prepare 2nd V. fischeri ES114 culture.
Keep inflow water paused for ~3 hours.

steps.title: Prepare prey culture (Day 0)
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette, fill two 125 mL flasks with 50 mL PP25 medium each. Label each flask with “V. fischeri ES114 – Step 3 – <date>”.

steps.title: Inoculate prey flasks with V. fischeri
steps.instruction: From a –80 °C stock of V. fischeri ES114, collect a glob of frozen culture (≈½ grain of rice) with a sterile toothpick, swirl it into each flask, and place the used toothpick into a “dirties” beaker for later autoclaving.

steps.title: Incubate prey cultures overnight
steps.instruction: Incubate the two 125 mL flasks shaking at 85 rpm, 28 °C for ~16 h (overnight).

steps.title: Amplify Halobacteriovorax (Day 2)
steps.instruction: When clearing is first visible, verify turbidity, inoculate predator, prepare larger flasks, and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add a label to one of the 125 mL flasks (the one that will receive Halobacteriovorax) with “Halobacteriovorax sp. GFR8 – Step 4 – <date>”. Both flasks should be visibly turbid; if not, repeat the inoculation of V. fischeri or check the –80 °C stock.

Inoculate the labeled 125 mL flask with Halobacteriovorax sp. GFR8 from a –80 °C stock: use a sterile toothpick to collect a glob of predator culture, swirl it in the flask, and place the stick in the “dirties” beaker. Do NOT add V. fischeri to this flask (control).
Using a serological pipette, fill two 500 mL flasks with 250 mL PP25 each. Label each with “V. fischeri ES114 – Step 5 – <date>”.
Inoculate each 500 mL flask with V. fischeri ES114 from the –80 °C stock (same toothpick method as above). Place each used stick in the “dirties” beaker.
Incubate the two 500 mL flasks shaking at 85 rpm, 28 °C overnight (~16 h).

Add a label to one of the 500 mL flasks that will receive Halobacteriovorax with “Halobacteriovorax sp. GFR8 – Step 6 – <date>”. Both 500 mL flasks should be visibly turbid; if not, repeat the V. fischeri inoculation or check the stock.
Incubate the Halobacteriovorax‑inoculated 125 mL flask together with the two 500 mL V. fischeri flasks shaking at 85 rpm, 28 °C for 24 h (or 48–72 h for the 500 mL flasks, as indicated).

steps.title: Filter predator culture
steps.instruction: Pass the cleared Halobacteriovorax sp. GFR8 culture (from the 125 mL flask) through a 0.45 µm filter using a vacuum pump with filter columns (preferred over syringe filters). The filtrate should be clear and contain only Halobacteriovorax cells.

steps.title: Prepare aquarium inoculation (Day 3)
steps.instruction: Pause water flow and new water input to the aquarium, note the time, then add the filtered predator culture at a 1:75 culture‑to‑tank ratio.

substeps.instruction: Using sterile beakers, remove 10 % of the tank volume (≈1 L from a 2.5‑gallon tank) and discard.
While wearing fresh gloves, spray the work area thoroughly with ≥75 % ethanol, wipe with a Kim‑wipe, and discard the wipe. Repeat this disinfection each time cultures are handled.
Calculate the required predator volume: for a 2.5‑gallon tank add 125 mL of filtered Halobacteriovorax sp. GFR8 culture (1 part culture : 75 parts water).
Transfer the calculated volume (125 mL) of filtered Halobacteriovorax culture into the aquarium.
If contamination occurs, perform all subsequent culturing steps inside a biosafety hood.

steps.title: Dispose of cultures and clean equipment
steps.instruction: Bleach all bacterial cultures before disposal. Wash reusable equipment with soap and water, then autoclave. Discard the used toothpicks in the “dirties” beaker for autoclaving.

substeps.instruction: Discard the 125 mL and 500 mL cultures (steps 3–6) by bleaching, washing, and autoclaving.
After filtrate collection, discard the remaining culture residues in the same manner.
